tasks.prompt: Explain how a runtime call to magic_enum::enum_name(value) produces the enum's name string: what internal steps and functions are involved, from the call to the returned string_view?
tasks.success_criterion: Describes that enum_name(value) uses enum_index to find the index, then returns names_v[index]; names_v is a constexpr array built from enum_name_v<E,V>, which extracts the name via compile-time reflection.
tasks.answer_key: enum_name(value) -> detail::enum_index<D,S>(value) yields the index -> returns detail::names_v<D,S>[*index]. names_v is built by detail::names(index_sequence) from enum_name_v<E, values_v[J]>. enum_name_v<E,V> computes the name at compile time via reflection (detail::n<V>() parsing __PRETTY_FUNCTION__/__FUNCSIG__), with customize-hook support.
tasks.notes: explain — comprehension of the reflection pipeline; judge-graded against the reference answer.
